p.t: Get a free US company tax number, the EIN, from the IRS first. Use only the official IRS website and never pay a website for it.

Get a state sales tax certificate only if your state has sales tax and suppliers ask for one.
Keep a W-9 form ready for suppliers who accept it.

Do your paperwork before you contact suppliers, where you can.
Rules differ by state and by supplier, so ask each supplier what it requires.

Fill out a **W-9** (a US tax form) when a supplier asks for one.
Get an **EIN** (a free US tax number for your business) before you contact suppliers.

**Ask** each supplier what they need, instead of guessing.
Check the **MAP** rule (the lowest price you may show) before you offer coupons.
Which tax numbers apply to you
p.s: EIN, tax IDs and supplier paperwork

p.t: **US business**
What applies: An EIN (Employer Identification Number, a free US company tax number) is required. It comes from the IRS (Internal Revenue Service, the US federal tax office).
A sales tax certificate (a state permit for buying without paying sales tax when you resell) applies where your state has sales tax and suppliers ask for one.
**Non-US resident starting a US business**
What applies: Apply for an EIN through the international route (the IRS process for people living outside the US).
An ITIN (Individual Taxpayer Identification Number, a tax number for people without a Social Security number, or SSN) is used for tax filing without an SSN.

**European business not selling into the US**
What applies: A VAT number (Value Added Tax number, the European sales tax number) is enough. An EIN is not needed.

**Canadian seller**
What applies: Sources disagree (see Conflicts below).
**Store that does not sell in the US**
What applies: No EIN is needed for that store.
1. **Get the EIN from the IRS first.** It is the minimum you need before you contact suppliers.
p.h: Decision order: what to get and when

p.t: 2. **Get a sales tax certificate if your state has sales tax and suppliers ask for one.**
3. **Keep a W-9 ready for suppliers that accept one.** A W-9 is an IRS form that gives a supplier your tax details.
4. **Apply before you contact suppliers, where possible.** Some suppliers require these documents and others do not.
5. **If you are close to approval, have the documents ready within one to two weeks.** Do not wait and contact the supplier again later.
The core numbers and what they are (continued)
p.s: EIN, tax IDs and supplier paperwork

p.t: The core numbers and what they are

An **EIN** (Employer Identification Number) is a **9-digit** number the IRS issues to a business.
It works like a Social Security number for the company.

You give it to suppliers instead of your personal SSN.
The format is **two digits, a dash and seven digits**.
A tax ID in that format is the same kind of number as an EIN.

It is a federal tax ID, which means a US national tax number.
It is **free** from the IRS.

It is needed for tax reporting and for many business tasks in the US.
A US business typically **needs an EIN** for tax filings.
A US business also needs an EIN to open a business bank account.
An EIN is needed to open a business bank account, apply for business licenses, file business taxes and fill in most supplier application forms.

It keeps business tax and accounting records separate from personal records.
**Do not** use your Social Security number in place of an EIN.

Using the EIN keeps business and personal finances separate.
US business suppliers require an EIN.
Many suppliers ask for an EIN during approval.
Suppliers prefer an EIN over a personal SSN.
Suppliers may use the EIN and the sales tax ID (your state's sales tax number) as interchangeable terms, meaning the same thing, when they request a tax ID. See Conflicts below.
Sales tax certificate, resale certificate and related names
p.s: EIN, tax IDs and supplier paperwork

p.t: A **sales tax certificate** (a state permit for buying without paying sales tax when you resell) is the same thing as a

reseller permit.
A sales tax certificate and a resale certificate are the same document, not two separate ones.

They can be obtained online, state by state.
The process is typically fast and automated.
A **sales tax permit** and a reseller certificate are the same thing.
They are based on the EIN and cover collecting and remitting sales tax (collecting sales tax from buyers and paying it to the state).

Suppliers asking for either one are requesting the same document.
In the US, a reseller permit and a sales tax certificate are the **same document**.

In many states, a sales tax license and a resale certificate are the same document.
Suppliers may ask for either one.

A resale certificate and a sales tax ID refer to the same thing.
Use them interchangeably when registering for sales tax.
A reseller number is essentially a sales tax ID.

Some suppliers ask for it, and depending on your state you may need one.
A **seller's permit** is also called a sales tax permit, sales tax license or reseller's permit.

A business license, sales tax certificate and sales tax registration number usually refer to the same thing.
The name varies by state.
A supplier's request for a business license number generally means the same thing as a reseller permit or sales tax ID.
Names differ by state. **Search** for the state name plus "sales tax certificate" or "resale certificate."
The W-9 is an IRS form that a US business uses to request the taxpayer identification number of a US-based supplier or contractor.

It collects this information in a standard format.
It applies only when the business pays US-based payees (the people or companies you pay).
A W-9 is usually **not needed**, but fill it out if a supplier asks for it.
An **ITIN** (Individual Taxpayer Identification Number) is a tax ID for individuals, meaning people rather than companies.

It is for people who are not US citizens or residents and need to file US taxes.
Use it when you are a non-US resident starting a US business.

An ITIN is used **only** for non-US citizens filing taxes without a Social Security number.
For non-US residents, an ITIN works similarly to an EIN.

Suppliers may ask for one or the other.
**Ask each supplier** what they require.
Check forums and communities for answers.
VAT and corporate tax numbers
p.s: EIN, tax IDs and supplier paperwork

p.t:
VAT is specific to Europe. (2024 advice)
An EIN is specific to the US. (2024 advice)

A **VAT number is enough** for European business. (2024 advice)
A corporate tax number is not the same as a VAT number.

Suppliers may ask for a specific one before approving (authorizing) a store.
**Ask which number** a supplier requires before you submit the application. This avoids delays.
Getting your EIN
An EIN is **free** on the official IRS website (irs.gov).
Many third-party sites (outside companies, not the government) charge for the same EIN. Use only official sources.

A third-party service is **not needed**.
Some companies charge about $200 or more for the same free filing.

Paid services that advertise EIN setup are unnecessary for US residents.
Non-residents may need paid help to obtain one.

Paid helpers are **not needed** for this simple process.
Many online ads charge fees to do these steps for you.
**Procedure: free EIN in the US**

1. **Search** for "EIN number" on Google.
2. **Do not click** the paid results marked as ads. These companies charge a fee for setting up an EIN.

3. **Click the first organic result** (the normal, unpaid result), which is the IRS site at irs.gov.
4. **Apply** for the EIN online and answer the questions the IRS asks. No paid helper is needed.

5. Expect to receive the EIN typically within about **15 minutes**.
**Procedure: apply for an EIN**
1. **Use only the IRS website**, not paid third-party services.

2. If you live outside the US, use the international applicant route, which requires a phone call.
3. **Check the IRS phone hours** before calling.

**Procedure: apply for an EIN**
1. **Go to the IRS website** and apply for an employer identification number (EIN) for free.

2. The application takes about **five minutes**.
3. **Do not pay** a third-party service for the EIN. Some companies charge about $200 or more for the same free filing.
4. **Use the EIN** instead of your social security number when applying for supplier accounts.
How long it takes
p.s: EIN, tax IDs and supplier paperwork

p.t:
5 to 10 minutes, number received immediately on completion
About 10 minutes online

**About five minutes**: (2024),
5 to 10 minutes, 9-digit EIN produced
5 to 10 minutes
About 15 minutes online

About 15 minutes, received typically within this time
An online EIN application usually takes **5 to 10 minutes**.
It produces a 9-digit EIN.
The IRS online EIN application **only works during IRS business hours**, even though it is an online form.

If you try early in the morning or late at night, it may not be available.
**Plan the application for business hours.**
**Get the EIN as early as possible.**
It is free on the IRS website, is required by many suppliers, and takes about **10 minutes** online.
An LLC (limited liability company, a registered company that keeps business and personal money apart) is the company type you may form.

Here it is only mentioned as a timing point.
**Apply for your EIN** directly on the IRS website after your LLC is officially approved.

An EIN can be obtained without an LLC.
When reaching out to suppliers without an LLC yet, get an EIN from the IRS website for free in about **five minutes**.
**Form an LLC first** only if you want to give company details at the time of approval.

Not having an LLC or S-Corp (a US tax setup for small companies) usually does not affect supplier approvals.
This had never been seen happen.

A business license and insurance are **optional** for an online store.
However, **get an EIN at a minimum** if you do business in the US.
Sole proprietors
p.s: EIN, tax IDs and supplier paperwork

p.t: A **sole proprietor** (one person running a business, with no company registered) can contact suppliers once the store is built.

No legal entity (a registered company or legal form) is needed for this.
A US business without a Social Security number can get an EIN from the IRS website.

**Get an EIN even as a sole proprietor.**
It is only needed for businesses in the US.

A sole proprietor without employees does not strictly need an EIN.
They can obtain one or use the owner's SSN instead.

A sole proprietor can be approved by some US suppliers, according to reports from store owners.
This was not verified.

An existing EIN from a previous business may be reusable for a new store.
The business type on the EIN may need updating.

**Verify with a tax professional** (an accountant or tax advisor) before reuse.
Reusing an old EIN from a business that never started is probably allowed.
**Verify it with a lawyer** or a legal forum before you do.
An EIN can be applied for directly by the company.
p.h: Who applies and how the form is filled

p.t: The title used on the form (president, CEO) is a matter of how you describe yourself.
A partnership (two or more owners) with several officers (company leaders with official titles) **requires more care**.
Pacing means the order and speed of your steps.
p.h: Why the EIN matters for pacing

p.t:
Tax documents, EIN and state registrations **can be completed after you start**. (2023 advice)
Many suppliers still approve new retailers without them. (2023 advice)

For a foreign founder, an EIN can take a long time, sometimes up to around **60 days**.
**Keep building the store** and contacting suppliers in the meantime.
**Hold back** top-tier suppliers (the highest-level, most important ones) until your business documents are complete.
Applying from outside the US (continued)
p.s: EIN, tax IDs and supplier paperwork

p.t: Applying from outside the US

**Non-US citizens must call the IRS** to apply.
US citizens can apply online at irs.gov.

Non-US residents cannot get an EIN online and must call the IRS.
Their process still begins at IRS.gov.
A non-US resident can get an EIN on the IRS website, though a phone call may be part of the process.
Non-US applicants can get an EIN by calling the IRS international applicant number listed on the IRS EIN page. (2023 advice)

US citizens can use the same online process. (2023 advice)
Applicants outside the US may be directed to call in instead of applying online.

**Check the foreign applicant route** before applying.
Non-US businesses can apply for the equivalent tax identification number on the same site.
To obtain a US resale certificate as a non-US resident, **form a US business entity first** and apply through that entity. (2024 advice)

A virtual address (a mail-only address with no office) is **not enough**. (2024 advice)
A **real company address is required**. (2024 advice)
Stripe Atlas (an online service that sets up US companies) was named as one common formation service. (2024 advice)
A state-issued resale certificate, not Stripe Atlas, is what suppliers usually ask for. (2024 advice)
See the international applicant procedure under Getting your EIN above.
Canadian sellers
p.s: EIN, tax IDs and supplier paperwork

p.t: A Canadian seller **does not need an EIN**, because it is an IRS number for US businesses.
A Canadian business selling into the US probably needs a US tax ID.
This is a FEIN (Federal Employer Identification Number, the same as an EIN) that can be obtained online from the IRS.
This is not certain. **Confirm it** with Canadians who already run US businesses or with a tax professional.

Some US suppliers ask Canadian sellers for an EIN or federal tax ID.
This requires a short call to the IRS.
Requirements differ by brand, so **check with other Canadian sellers** in community forums.

A business registered in Canada can get a US EIN from the IRS by phone. (2025 advice)
It **should not get a resale certificate first**. (2025 advice)
When an application asks for one, leave that section blank.
Or state that the business is based in Canada and has no nexus (a legal link to a US state, such as an office, staff or enough sales, that makes you owe its sales tax) in any US state. (2025 advice)
A state tax ID and resale certificate follow later, once a state threshold (a sales amount that starts the duty to register) is reached. (2025 advice)
A foreign entity (a company registered outside the US) without a nexus in any US state probably **does not need a sales tax certificate**.
This is not verified. **Submit the supplier application** and check whether approval requires it.
**Do not collect resale certificates** for states where you have no obligation, just because a supplier asks for one.

Only obtain them for states where you have physical presence (a real office, staff or stock there).
Or where you crossed the sales threshold in a year.
Sales tax certificate and state resale documents (continued)
p.s: EIN, tax IDs and supplier paperwork

p.t: Sales tax certificate and state resale documents

A sales tax certificate is **required by most suppliers** if your state has a sales tax.
If your state has no sales tax, **you do not need one**.

A sales tax certificate is needed only if the supplier requires it and the business is in a state that has sales tax.
In states without sales tax, no certificate is needed.

In other states, the certificate can be applied for online in about **10 to 15 minutes**.
Some suppliers ask for a state sales tax certificate and some do not.

Requirements depend on the state where the business is based.
Having the certificate does no harm and is required in some states.

Whether you need a resale certificate depends on the supplier and on your state.
Some suppliers ask for one and others do not, and some states do not issue them.
Before a state's sales tax threshold is reached, you usually **do not need a tax certificate** in that state.

Many suppliers ask for a seller's permit or sales tax certificate, but not all do.
Requirements are state specific. States without sales tax do not need a certificate there.
For each state, **look up the state's reseller certificate**. (2023 advice)
The certificate allows collecting and remitting sales tax and is required by most suppliers. (2023 advice)

In a state where the business is based, a sales tax certificate is required.
Suppliers may ask for a tax-exempt form (a form that says a purchase is not taxed).
The tax-exempt certificate usually requires an existing sales tax certificate.
Whether suppliers require an EIN and a sales tax ID before approval varies by supplier and by state.
When you need one (continued)
p.s: EIN, tax IDs and supplier paperwork

p.t:
**Ask each supplier directly** rather than assuming the same requirement.
Some suppliers ask for a resale certificate and others do not.

**Ask each supplier** before assuming you need one.
**Get a resale certificate early**, since many suppliers ask for one even though not all do. (2026 advice)
Requirements depend on the state where you do business. (2026 advice)
**Apply for a state resale certificate or sales tax permit early**, as suppliers often ask for it when you are approved. (2025 advice)
**Do not apply for resale permits** in every state a supplier asks for if you have no sales nexus there. (2025 advice)
**Offer a W-9 instead**, along with your home-state resale certificate. (2025 advice)
**Provide a resale certificate** for the state where your business operates when a supplier asks for one. (2023 advice)

Do not treat the certificate as a general document for every state. (2023 advice)
Get a sales tax certificate and an EIN tax ID **eventually**.

Obtaining them sooner rather than later avoids delays with suppliers that ask for them.
A reseller number is **not urgent** in the early stage.
Purchases from suppliers are not taxed when you resell. (2025 advice)
The reason: you give the supplier a W-9 if requested, or your sales tax certificate (also called a resale certificate). (2025 advice)
Sales tax is separate from income tax. (2025 advice)
Getting a state certificate
p.s: EIN, tax IDs and supplier paperwork

p.t: **Procedure: sales tax certificate (general)**
1. **Search Google** for "[Your State] sales tax certificate." Use only official.gov websites (government web addresses ending in.gov). Do not pay third-party sites.
2. Complete online registration if your state offers it. Most do, and it is often free.

3. You will receive a downloadable PDF (a file you can print) or a physical certificate by mail.
**Procedure: resale or sales tax certificate** (2023 advice)

1. **Go to your state's.gov website.**
2. **Search** for "[Your State] resale certificate" or "[Your State] sales tax certificate."

3. **Complete the online form** (typically about **5 minutes**).
4. **Receive your certificate number.**

5. **Provide this number** to suppliers to purchase at wholesale (buying at the trade price) without sales tax.
**Procedure: resale certificate** (2025 advice)

1. **Search Google** for the registration state plus sales tax certificate or resale certificate.
2. **Open the official.gov page** of that state.
3. **Complete the online form.** Many states give a PDF immediately. Some mail it, which can take about a week.

4. **Get it before supplier outreach**, because some suppliers require it and others do not.
**Procedure: sales tax certificate online**

In a state with sales tax, **search** for the state name plus sales tax certificate or reseller certificate.
Then apply through the state's online form.

**Procedure: sales tax ID after your EIN**
**Get a sales tax ID after your EIN**, as early as practical, because many suppliers ask for it.

The setup is usually done online. States without sales tax do not need one.
**Procedure: when a supplier asks for a resale number and the state has no certificate**
1. **Search** for an exemption form (a form showing you are not charged sales tax) on the official state government website.

2. If none is listed, **call or email** the state's contact number and ask for a document stating you are exempt.
3. **Send that document** to the supplier.

**Procedure: resale certificate in a state with no registration yet**
1. **Ask the accountant** for the exact name of the state sales and use tax form (the form for reporting sales tax).

2. **Search that form name** online to check whether it can be filed online.
3. If it is available online, **file it there** instead of visiting a city or county office.
Multi-state and specific states
p.s: EIN, tax IDs and supplier paperwork

p.t: **Do not apply for resale permits** in every state a supplier asks for if you have no sales nexus there.

**Offer a W-9 instead**, along with your home-state resale certificate.
A seller's permit is required in your own home state, and most suppliers will ask for it.
You generally do not need a permit in every state, although some suppliers may request one per state.
A supplier that does not receive a Florida annual resale certificate may offer to charge **7% Florida sales tax** on orders shipped within Florida. (2023 advice)
Or it may refuse shipments to Florida. (2023 advice)
**Send your home-state resale certificate first.** State that you have no economic nexus (a legal link to a state created by sales volume alone) in Florida. (2023 advice)

Resale certificate rules differ by state. (2024 advice)
A business formed in Delaware may not need a sales tax certificate, because Delaware has no sales tax. (2024 advice)
A Delaware wholesaler license (a permit to buy at wholesale) was mentioned as an option for businesses set up there. (2024 advice)

For a business in Delaware, the supplier example is handled with a W-9 instead.
See the procedure under What to tell suppliers.
A W-9 is a US tax form that gives your tax details to a business. IRS means the US tax agency.
Fill out a W-9 **when a supplier asks for one.**
p.h: When and how to use a W-9

p.t: Give a W-9 **if requested**, or your sales tax certificate (a state document with your sales tax number), when purchasing for resale (buying items to sell again). (2025 advice)
Offer a W-9 **instead of applying for resale permits** in states where you have no nexus (a legal tie to a state, such as an office or enough sales there).
Send it together with your home-state resale certificate (a state form that proves you buy to resell). (2025 advice)
A D&B (Dun & Bradstreet, a company that gives business ID numbers) number **is not necessary** for the business.

**Procedure: handling a W-9 request from a large business customer**
1. Keep a blank Form W-9 PDF in the PDF files section of the corporate information board.

2. When a customer asks for it, **print the form.**
3. Fill in the business name and the tax information.
4. **Send** the completed form to the customer.
5. Keep the file ready because large companies request it repeatedly.
What to tell suppliers
p.s: EIN, tax IDs and supplier paperwork

p.t: Suppliers are the companies that provide the products you sell.
**Ask** each supplier directly what they require before assuming a requirement.
**Get the EIN** (Employer Identification Number, a free US tax number for a business from the IRS) before contacting suppliers.

The EIN is the **minimum** to have before contacting suppliers.
**Get a resale certificate** before supplier outreach, since some suppliers require it.
EIN numbers and resale certificate numbers are needed for supplier applications. (2023 advice)
D-U-N-S numbers (business ID numbers from Dun & Bradstreet) are **not required** for this model. This model means dropshipping, where the supplier ships each order straight to the customer.
(2023 advice)
**Ask** which number a supplier requires: a corporate tax number (the tax ID of a company) or a VAT number (value added tax, a sales tax used in many countries outside the US),
before submitting the application.
Provide the official **LLC** name (limited liability company, a business type that separates your personal money from business debts)
and the business address where the LLC is registered. Do **not** give a private mailing address.

The company name and EIN go on supplier approval forms, which usually ask for company details in a **one-page form**.
The company name is **not shown to customers.**

One LLC can run **several stores.**
When calling suppliers, use the **store name.**
On approval forms, list the store names you will sell under, next to the corporation's legal name.
Provide a resale certificate for the state where your business operates **when a supplier asks for one.** (2023 advice)
What to give the supplier (continued)
p.s: EIN, tax IDs and supplier paperwork

p.t: EIN numbers and resale certificate numbers are needed for supplier applications. (2023 advice)
**Procedure: when a supplier asks for a state tax certificate** (a state document with your sales tax number) **and your state does not issue one** (2024 advice)
1. Contact the supplier, asking for their tax certificate requirement.
2. If they ask for a state tax certificate, start with your business registration state (e.g., Delaware).
3. If your state does not issue a sales tax certificate (e.g., Delaware), **provide a W9 form** from the IRS instead.

4. Tell the supplier: "I am a Delaware business; please see the attached W9."
5. **Ask** if the W9 is acceptable.
6. If not, follow up with any documents your state requires.
Suppliers typically request **credit** (letting you pay later, after you get the goods)

and banking information as part of the retailer approval process.
Use a **business credit card or debit card** for authorization, not bank account details. This keeps privacy and control.
Leave the business references (other companies that vouch for you) **blank** if you are not applying for credit.
Use **cash or a credit card only**, since no credit terms are needed in the dropshipping model. (2023 advice)
Drop shipping stores **do not require credit** for supplier approval.
A low credit score (a number that shows how well you pay debts) caused by past insolvency or bankruptcy (failing to pay your debts) **does not block** working with suppliers.
D&B numbers are **not required** for this model.
Supplier agreements and dropship policy
p.s: EIN, tax IDs and supplier paperwork

p.t: For **high-ticket items** (expensive products, $5,000+), you can request a supplier agreement (a written deal

between you and the supplier).
**Search** "dropshipping supplier agreement" on Google, or check competitor sites (other stores selling similar products) for templates to adapt.
The Source A material does not provide standard agreement forms.

You do **not need** your own dropship policy (a written rules document for dropshipping). (2024 advice)
Suppliers that ask for one are **rare.** (2024 advice)
A **simple agreement** from a template is enough. (2024 advice)
Conflict: says high-ticket suppliers may ask for a supplier agreement, while says a dropship policy is rarely requested.
**Use a template agreement for high-ticket suppliers**, and a simple agreement otherwise.
On a supplier price sheet (the list of prices the supplier gives you),
**MSRP** is the manufacturer's suggested retail price (the price the maker recommends),
while **MAP** is the minimum advertised price (the lowest price you may show a product at). (2023 advice)
**Check the case pack size** (how many units come in one set), since the wholesale cost (the price you pay the supplier) may cover a set of several units rather than one. (2023 advice)

Some markets have **no legally enforceable MAP** (no law makes the rule binding), but suppliers may follow unwritten rules.
Discounting **can reduce their supply.**
In the UK, undercutting (selling below) a supplier's price can cause the supply to dry up, because of damage to the supplier's reputation with other retailers.
MAP compliance (following the MAP rule) is judged by the **price displayed on the store**,

not by the price after a coupon (a discount code).
A coupon at checkout (the payment step) is usually allowed.
A displayed price below MAP is a **violation** (breaking the rule) unless the supplier agreement permits it.
**Check the supplier's MAP agreement before offering coupon codes.**
A 20 dollar coupon on a 200 dollar MAP product is allowed **as long as the product page still shows 200 dollars.**
Conflicts between sources
p.s: EIN, tax IDs and supplier paperwork

p.t:
**EIN and sales tax ID (a state number for collecting sales tax)**
Position A: Interchangeable terms when a supplier requests a tax ID.
Position B: Separate: an EIN does not replace a resale certificate ID, and the EIN is free from the IRS while the reseller permit comes from the state.,

When each applies: **Treat them as separate documents:** the EIN is federal, the resale certificate is state-issued.
**Business license (a general permit to run a business)**

Position A: Optional for an online store.
Position B: Generally the same as a reseller permit or sales tax ID when a supplier asks for it. (2024 advice)
When each applies: Optional for the store itself. **If a supplier asks for a business license number, provide the reseller permit or sales tax ID.**

**Sole proprietor EIN (one person running a business alone)**
Position A: Not strictly needed.
Position B: **Get one** even as a sole proprietor.

When each applies: Get one as the lower-risk option, since suppliers prefer an EIN.
**Start point for EIN**
Position A: Apply after the LLC is approved.
Position B: Can be obtained without an LLC, and suppliers can be contacted before forming one.,

When each applies: **Apply after the LLC if you have one.** Otherwise apply without one, since the EIN is the minimum before supplier contact.
**Time for EIN**

Position A: About **5 minutes.**
Position B: About **10 to 15 minutes.**
When each applies: Plan for 5 to 15 minutes, and apply during IRS business hours.

**Canadian sellers**
Position A: No EIN needed, since it is for US businesses.
Position B: US tax ID probably needed. EIN may be requested by some suppliers.

When each applies: **Check with the supplier.** Give the EIN if asked, by phone, without a resale certificate first.
**High-ticket supplier agreements**

Position A: Can request a supplier agreement.
Position B: Suppliers asking for a dropship policy are rare. (2024 advice)

When each applies: High-ticket suppliers: **use a template agreement.** Others: a simple agreement is enough.
**Non-US EIN route (for people outside the US)**

Position A: Non-US residents must call.
Position B: Non-US residents may apply online on the IRS website, with a phone call possibly part of the process.
When each applies: **Check the foreign applicant route** on the IRS EIN page before applying.
The IRS EIN Number page is listed as a resource for obtaining a US Employer Identification Number (EIN) for a US-based business.

No further detail is given.
Applying for a seller's permit (a state permit to collect sales tax) typically requires your **SSN** (Social Security Number, your personal US ID) or **EIN.**
It is the **first paperwork step** before finding suppliers.
